newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: No ice problems on Rhine, some tributaries frozen.
newsitem.headline: No ice problems on Rhine, some tributaries frozen.

text.p: Barge traffic on the Rhine remained unaffected by the freezing weather in Europe, but ice was still causing problems on some tributaries and canals, Dutch water authorities and barge traders said on Thursday.
"There are no problems on the Rhine itself in either Germany or the Netherlands at the moment," a spokesman at water inspectors RIZA said.
However, there were blockages on some Rhine tributaries, with particular problems in the Ruhr area, which had squeezed barge tariffs up by around five percent, a barge trader said.
But he said charterers were still managing to find ways to get barges through. "There are still alternatives," he said.
In the Netherlands, ice on the IJsselmeer meant that shipping was restricted to occasional convoys, he said.
Amsterdam-Rotterdam barge routes were in reasonable condition, but there were problems with ice around locks on Rotterdam-Antwerp canals and waterways.
